Problem: PAC learning with classification noise
Main Contribution: Pioneered PAC bounds under random classification noise; proved sample complexity inflation of O(1/(1-2eta)^2)
Known Limitation: Limited to binary concepts and uniform noise rates

Problem: Statistical Query Model under Noise
Main Contribution: Proved that any concept class learnable in SQ model is learnable with classification noise
Known Limitation: Requires queries to distribution rather than individual samples

Problem: Convex potential boosters under label noise
Main Contribution: Proved that all convex potential boosters fail under random classification noise for linearly separable data
Known Limitation: Assumes convex potential loss function; does not address non-convex deep nets

Problem: Noise tolerance of polyhedral classifiers
Main Contribution: Proved that symmetric losses (e.g. 0-1, ramp loss) are inherently noise tolerant under risk minimization
Known Limitation: Optimization of non-convex symmetric losses is NP-hard in general

Problem: Learning with Noisy Labels
Noise Assumption: Conditionally independent given true label Y
Main Contribution: Introduced backward unbiased loss correction ell_corr = T^-1 ell; established finite-sample excess risk bounds
Known Limitation: Assumes exact knowledge of transition matrix T; backward loss can produce negative risk values

Problem: Classification with Asymmetric Label Noise
Main Contribution: Formulated label noise as mutual contamination; established minimax optimal rates for transition probabilities
Known Limitation: Requires irreducible component distributions; high sample complexity in high dimensions

Problem: Learning with Symmetric Label Noise: The Importance of Convexity
Main Contribution: Proved that the unhinged linear loss is the unique convex loss function that is strictly noise-tolerant under symmetric noise
Known Limitation: Unhinged loss has no lower bound; sensitive to outliers and optimization instability

Problem: Making Deep Neural Networks Robust to Label Noise: A Loss Correction Approach
Noise Assumption: P(Y_tilde | X, Y) = P(Y_tilde | Y); anchor points exist
Method: Forward and Backward loss correction via anchor points
Main Contribution: Showed how to estimate T using network softmax predictions on confident anchor points; proved forward/backward risk convergence
Known Limitation: Anchor point assumption often violated in real-world high-entropy classes

Problem: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
Main Contribution: Demonstrated that overparameterized deep networks have sufficient capacity to fit 100% random labels with zero training error
Known Limitation: Did not propose a noise-mitigation method; purely empirical diagnosis

Problem: A Closer Look at Memorization in Deep Networks
Main Contribution: Discovered early-learning phenomenon: neural networks learn real, clean patterns first before memorizing noisy labels
Known Limitation: Qualitative analysis without formal sample complexity bounds

Problem: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
Main Contribution: Identified miscalibration in modern deep networks and popularized Expected Calibration Error (ECE) and Temperature Scaling
Known Limitation: Focused strictly on clean training data without label corruptions

Problem: Generalized Cross Entropy Loss for Training Deep Neural Networks with Noisy Labels
Main Contribution: Developed GCE (L_q loss) interpolating between Cross Entropy (q->0) and MAE (q=1) with negative Box-Cox transformation
Known Limitation: Requires tuning hyperparameter q; performance degrades under extreme asymmetric noise

Problem: Co-teaching: Robust Training of Deep Neural Networks with Extremely Noisy Labels
Main Contribution: Introduced Co-teaching where two networks peer-filter small-loss samples for each other to avoid confirmation bias
Known Limitation: Double computational cost (trains two models); can discard hard clean samples

Problem: Symmetric Cross Entropy for Robust Learning with Noisy Labels
Main Contribution: Introduced Reverse Cross Entropy (RCE) and proved SCE is robust to symmetric label noise while maintaining gradient flow
Known Limitation: Requires alpha/beta weighting balancing; reverse cross entropy can suffer from underfitting

Problem: On Symmetric Losses for Learning from Corrupted Labels
Main Contribution: Proved that symmetric losses are strictly noise-tolerant under symmetric noise but not inherently under asymmetric noise
Known Limitation: Demonstrated severe optimization degradation of pure symmetric losses (MAE) on complex datasets

Problem: Are Anchor Points Really Indispensable in Label-Noise Learning?
Noise Assumption: Transition matrix T exists without anchor points
Method: Dual T-Estimator / Slack transition matrix estimation
Main Contribution: Introduced intermediate transition matrix estimation without requiring extreme anchor points via slack variables
Known Limitation: Adds optimization complexity and additional hyperparameter tuning

Problem: On the Efficacy of Mixup for Reducing Ambiguity and Miscalibration
Method: Mixup training for calibration under noise
Main Contribution: Demonstrated that Mixup regularisation prevents noisy label memorisation and reduces Expected Calibration Error (ECE)
Known Limitation: Does not explicitly correct for asymmetric transition matrices

Problem: DivideMix: Learning with Noisy Labels as Semi-Supervised Learning
Method: DivideMix (GMM per-sample loss modeling + MixMatch SSL)
Main Contribution: State-of-the-art semi-supervised framework fitting a 2-component GMM on per-sample losses to divide data into clean and noisy sets
Known Limitation: Extremely heavy training pipeline (2 networks + warm-up + MixMatch + Co-refinement)

Problem: Confident Learning: Estimating Uncertainty in Dataset Labels
Noise Assumption: Joint distribution P(Y_tilde, Y*) estimable from out-of-sample predicted probabilities
Main Contribution: Formulated Confident Learning to directly estimate the joint distribution of noisy and true labels; open-source Cleanlab
Known Limitation: Pruning can discard valid edge cases; requires reliable out-of-sample probability estimates

Problem: Learning with Bounded Instance- and Label-Dependent Label Noise
Noise Assumption: P(Y_tilde | X, Y) depends directly on feature representation X
Main Contribution: Formalized instance-dependent noise bounds and proved conditions under which surrogate risk minimization preserves Bayes optimality
Known Limitation: Assumes bounded noise rate upper bound eta(x) < 1/2 across entire input space

Problem: Learning with Noisy Labels Revisited: A Study on ImageNet and CIFAR-10N
Method: Human noise benchmark and empirical evaluation of existing methods
Main Contribution: Released CIFAR-10N/100N human-annotated noisy benchmark; demonstrated that methods tuned for synthetic noise degrade on real noise
Known Limitation: Empirical dataset and benchmarking paper without novel theoretical risk bounds

Problem: Learning from Noisy Labels with Deep Neural Networks: A Survey
Main Contribution: Comprehensive IEEE TPAMI survey categorizing robust losses, loss correction, sample selection, and robust architectures
Known Limitation: Survey paper; does not introduce a standalone novel algorithm

Problem: Detecting Corrupted Labels Without Training a Model to Minimize Empirical Risk
Method: Cluster-based and topological label corruption detection
Main Contribution: Proved that label noise creates local topological inconsistencies in feature space detectable without full model training
Known Limitation: Relies on quality of self-supervised representation features

Problem: Normalized Loss Functions for Deep Learning with Noisy Labels
Main Contribution: Demonstrated that normalizing any loss function makes it symmetric and thus robust to symmetric noise
Known Limitation: Passive loss term can slow down early training convergence

Problem: Identifying Mislabeled Data using the Area Under the Margin Ranking
Main Contribution: Introduced AUM metric tracking difference between correct logit and maximal other logit across epochs to identify corrupted labels
Known Limitation: Requires full epoch logging of training logits; post-hoc identification
